messages.subject: INLA problem with optimization
parts:
Hello INLA group,
 
I am using INLA and the Lindgren et al. 2011's SPDE model into the preferential sampling problem according to Chapters 13-15 of the spde-tutorial.
In my cases, I assume three sets of samples with different preferentiality. messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA problem with optimization
parts:
I agree with Håvard. We have seen in LGCP that good priors are important
for the model to run at all!

If you think carefully about what the range and standard deviation means
for the spatial component in a point pattern, you may realise that they
are very hard things to infer.

You can try the new pc priors, see code below.

Also, please consider the 'corrected sd' after it finds the posterior mode
and hessian. This correction hints whether it has found the mode at all.

-----
sig0 = 0.5; rho0 = 0.3 #rho0 is typical range, sig0 typical sd
spde = local.inla.spde2.matern.new(mesh, prior.pc.rho = c(rho0, 0.5),
prior.pc.sig = c(sig0, 0.5))


local.inla.spde2.matern.new = function(mesh, alpha=2, prior.pc.rho,
prior.pc.sig)
{
# Call inla.spde2.matern with range and standard deviation
parametrization
d = INLA:::inla.ifelse(inherits(mesh, "inla.mesh"), 2, 1)
nu = alpha-d/2
kappa0 = log(8*nu)/2
tau0 = 0.5*(lgamma(nu)-lgamma(nu+d/2)-d/2*log(4*pi))-nu*kappa0
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh,
B.tau = cbind(tau0, nu, -1),
B.kappa = cbind(kappa0, -1, 0))

# Change prior information
param = c(prior.pc.rho, prior.pc.sig)
spde$f$hyper.default$theta1$prior = "pcspdega"
spde$f$hyper.default$theta1$param = param
spde$f$hyper.default$theta1$initial = log(prior.pc.rho[1])+1
spde$f$hyper.default$theta2$initial = log(prior.pc.sig[1])-1

# End and return
return(invisible(spde))
}

---

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
